# euvsimulator — EUV Lithography Simulator

An open-source EUV lithography simulator (Python/PyTorch, Apache-2.0) whose every physical
default has a named source. Version 2.2.1. It models the 13.5 nm imaging and resist chain on a
laptop; it is not a predictive tool for production resists, and the distance to the two named
measurement anchors is documented rather than tuned away.

## Links
- Repository: https://github.com/Flowbudget/euvsimulator
- Physics, sources, open questions: https://github.com/Flowbudget/euvsimulator/blob/main/docs/physics.md
- Documentation folder: https://github.com/Flowbudget/euvsimulator/tree/main/docs
- Notebooks (6, executed in CI): https://github.com/Flowbudget/euvsimulator/tree/main/notebooks
- Issues: https://github.com/Flowbudget/euvsimulator/issues
- Discussions: https://github.com/Flowbudget/euvsimulator/discussions

## What exists
- Mo/Si multilayer mirror (TMM, S-matrix, Névot-Croce roughness) and a CXRO f1/f2 database
- Mask diffraction: thin-mask by default, full RCWA 1D/2D on request (`use_rcwa=True`)
- Partially coherent aerial imaging (Abbe and Hopkins), conventional/annular/dipole/quasar pupils
- Resist chain: Dill ABC exposure, Gaussian SE blur, PEB kinetics fitted to Yamamoto 2011,
  Mack development with an Eikonal front and a vertical-column model
- Stochastics: Poisson shot noise, sampled PAG/quencher molecules, LER/LWR extraction
- Process window: Bossung curves, CD/NILS maps, DoF and EL, CSV/JSON export
- Calibration: wafer CD matrix to resist parameters (scipy, bootstrap CIs, uncertainty bands)
- Browser GUI and REST API (`euv serve`, FastAPI, no external assets)
- Modules present but not wired into the pipeline or CLI: `etch` (etch bias), `opc` (ILT bridge)

## What does not exist
There is no MCP server, no A2A agent endpoint and no hosted documentation site. Earlier versions
of this repository shipped manifests describing such services; they were removed in 2.2.1 because
no code backed them. The only interfaces are the Python API, the CLI and the local REST API.

## Getting started
```bash
pip install git+https://github.com/Flowbudget/euvsimulator.git
euv simulate --period 64 --cd 32 --dose 1.3 --resist-model full_chem
euv process-window --period 64 --cd 32
euv calibrate wafer.csv --period 44 --cd 22 --bands
euv serve            # browser GUI + REST API on http://127.0.0.1:8000/
```
CLI commands: `version`, `info`, `simulate`, `make-mask`, `process-window`, `materials`, `serve`,
`bench`, `calibrate`. Python 3.10 to 3.13.

## Python API
```python
from euvsimulator.pipeline import SimulationConfig, run_simulation

cfg = SimulationConfig(period_nm=64.0, line_width_nm=32.0, dose_mj_cm2=1.3,
                       resist_model="full_chem")   # defaults: na=0.33, sigma=0.8, grid=256
result = run_simulation(cfg)
print(result.cd_nm, result.nils_value, result.ler_nm, result.lwr_nm)
```
The default resist is the 2011 research resist of Yamamoto et al. and prints at about
1.3 mJ/cm² at 64 nm pitch. Named anchors live in `euvsimulator.presets`
(`nxe1716_config`, `met2d_config`).

## Testing
```bash
pip install -e ".[dev]"
pytest -q            # 989 tests as of 2.2.1
```
CI runs the suite on Linux, macOS and Windows with Python 3.10 to 3.13, plus ruff, mypy and the
six notebooks.

## Where contributions help
GPU acceleration for RCWA and imaging, validation against published measurements with a complete
parameter set, the MEEF weakness of the `aerial_threshold` model (documented in README under
known limitations), and temperature scaling for acid diffusion.
